md_description: Workflow for generating bacterial single amplified genome datasets from soil samples, including field collection, whole genome amplification, next-generation sequencing, and genome assembly. The pipeline preserves contextual metadata about sample collection site, environmental conditions, amplification kit, sequencing platform, and assembly algorithms to support ecological interpretation of bacterial diversity and functional potential in soil ecosystems.

soil_samples.reasoning: For the soil_samples Entity node, I included only intrinsic sample-origin and context fields that describe what the soil material is and where/under what conditions it was collected. I excluded process details (these belong to soil_collection), amplification, sequencing, and assembly fields because they are downstream operation/capture/derivative territory. I also avoided repeating any identifiers already generated elsewhere; since root-level sample identifiers are typically generated once, I used collection-site and environment descriptors rather than generic experiment/sample ID fields. The fields focus on the minimum metadata needed to interpret ecological provenance and compare soil samples across environments.

md_schema.descr: Name or label of the soil sampling location for this sample, recorded at collection time (for example, forest plot A, agricultural field 3, wetland transect 2). Use a stable site label rather than a protocol description. Type string.
Geographic latitude of the soil collection site in decimal degrees, recorded at or near the sampling point. Typical range -90 to 90. Use positive values for north and negative for south.
Geographic longitude of the soil collection site in decimal degrees, recorded at or near the sampling point. Typical range -180 to 180. Use positive values for east and negative for west.

Free-text description of the environmental conditions at the time of soil collection that are intrinsic to the sample provenance, such as moisture status, recent rainfall, vegetation cover, or land-use context. Record the observed field conditions, not instrument settings or later laboratory handling.

Broad soil type or texture category observed or assigned at collection time for the sampled material, used to contextualize bacterial habitat. Examples include sandy, loamy, clay-rich, organic-rich, or peat-like. Choose the closest field-validated descriptor.
Date when the soil sample was collected from the field. Use ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DD. This marks the provenance time point for the sample and is distinct from any later processing dates.

Immediate storage state of the soil sample after field collection and before downstream preparation, such as cooled, frozen, refrigerated, or ambient-held. Describe the sample's handling status only; do not include later laboratory processing steps.

soil_collection.reasoning: For the soil_collection Process node, I included only collection-operation metadata: how the field sampling was performed and what environmental observations were recorded during the act of collection. I excluded sample identity and provenance fields already owned by the soil_samples Entity node, and I excluded downstream handling, amplification, sequencing, and file/result fields because those belong to later nodes. I also included the operator role as required for operation nodes, but not sample properties. The fields are intended to let a downstream user reproduce or audit the collection event without duplicating the soil sample record.

md_schema.descr: Role of the person or team who performed the field soil collection event. For this workflow it should describe the collecting agent, typically researcher or field_technician, and is recorded at the time of sampling.

Field collection approach used to obtain the soil sample, recorded during the sampling event. Examples include core, scoop, auger, or shovel. This describes how the material was physically obtained, not the soil's intrinsic properties.

Depth below the soil surface from which the sample was collected, measured at collection time in centimeters. Typical range 0 to 200 cm depending on study design. Use the depth interval or a representative depth if the sample spans a horizon.

Ambient air temperature at the sampling site during soil collection, recorded at the time of collection. Typical range depends on site climate, often about -20 to 50 C. This is an observed environmental condition, not an instrument configuration.
Ambient relative humidity at the sampling site during soil collection, recorded at the time of collection. Typical range 0 to 100 percent. Use the field observation closest to the collection event.
Qualitative weather condition at the time of soil collection, recorded in the field to contextualize sampling conditions. Examples include clear, cloudy, rainy, snowy, windy, or mixed.

Short notes on access constraints or visible disturbance at the collection site that may affect interpretation of the sampled soil, such as compacted ground, recent tilling, erosion, or wildlife disturbance. Record only field observations made during the collection event.

prepared_soil_material.reasoning: For the prepared_soil_material Entity node, I included only intrinsic post-collection preparation state of the soil material that serves as input to whole genome amplification. I excluded collection-site provenance and ambient field conditions because those belong to the upstream soil_samples and soil_collection nodes, and I excluded amplification, sequencing, and assembly parameters because those are downstream. The fields capture how the soil material was stabilized or preprocessed before WGA, which is the key information a downstream user needs to interpret the input to the amplification step.

md_schema.descr: State of the soil material after field collection and basic handling, recorded immediately before whole genome amplification. Describe whether the material was untreated, sieved, homogenized, dried, or otherwise preconditioned. This captures the preparation stage rather than the field sampling event.

Upper or representative particle size fraction retained for the prepared soil material before amplification, measured or selected during basic handling in millimeters. Typical values may range from less than 0.1 to several millimeters depending on the protocol. Use the sieve cut or fraction used for downstream processing.

Temperature at which the prepared soil material was held between collection and whole genome amplification, measured during the storage interval. Typical range may be below 0 C for frozen storage or around 4 C for refrigerated storage. This is the post-collection holding condition for the material, not a field environmental measurement.

Elapsed time in hours between field collection/basic handling completion and the start of whole genome amplification. Typical range is 0 to several days depending on workflow. Record the interval for this prepared material, as it affects DNA integrity and downstream amplification performance.

Brief notes on visible condition or integrity of the prepared soil material before amplification, such as clumping, moisture level, contamination concern, or uniformity after handling. Use this to document material suitability for the downstream WGA step.

wga_process.reasoning: For the wga_process Process node, I included only parameters that define how whole genome amplification was performed and what kit/reagent configuration was used. I excluded soil provenance, prepared material properties, and all sequencing/assembly outputs because those belong to upstream Entity nodes or downstream Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also included the agent/software-equivalent operational detail appropriate for a process node: the amplification kit identity and version/lot where relevant. The fields are focused on reproducibility of the amplification step and on its immediate quality outcome, not on the amplified DNA product itself.

md_schema.descr: Name of the whole genome amplification kit used to amplify bacterial DNA from the soil-derived material. Record the commercial or protocol name exactly as used in the workflow, for example REPLI-g, MDA kit, or a custom WGA kit.
Manufacturer or supplier of the whole genome amplification kit used in this process. Record the vendor name as reported by the kit packaging or protocol documentation.
Kit version, catalog number, or lot number associated with the whole genome amplification reagent set used for this amplification run. Use this to disambiguate reagent formulations between runs.

Amount of soil-derived DNA input into the whole genome amplification reaction, measured at the start of the process in nanograms. Typical range may be fractions of a nanogram to tens of nanograms depending on protocol. Record the mass actually loaded into the reaction.
Total reaction volume used for the whole genome amplification reaction, measured in microliters at setup time. Typical range often lies between 10 and 50 uL depending on kit and protocol.

Incubation temperature used during the whole genome amplification reaction, recorded as the setpoint in degrees Celsius. Typical values depend on the kit, often around 30 C for MDA-like protocols. This is a process control parameter.
Total duration of the whole genome amplification incubation, measured in hours from reaction start to termination. Typical range may be 1 to 16 hours depending on protocol and kit.
Immediate quality assessment of the amplification reaction after completion, such as successful, low_yield, overamplified, or failed. Use this to capture the process-level outcome before sequencing.

amplified_dna.reasoning: For the amplified_dna Entity node, I included only intrinsic properties of the amplified DNA material after WGA and before sequencing. I excluded WGA kit/reaction parameters because those belong to the upstream wga_process node, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings and raw file properties because those belong downstream to ngs_capture and sequencing_reads. The fields focus on the identity, physical amount, storage, and preparation status of the amplified DNA so a user can assess what material entered sequencing.

md_schema.descr: Concentration of the whole-genome-amplified DNA material measured after amplification and before sequencing library preparation or capture. Report in nanograms per microliter. Typical range may be very low to hundreds of ng/uL depending on yield.

Total mass of amplified DNA recovered from the whole genome amplification reaction, measured after amplification and before sequencing. Report in nanograms. Typical range depends on kit and input amount, often spanning sub-ng to microgram levels.

Approximate fragment size distribution of the amplified DNA material before sequencing, measured or inferred after amplification and reported in base pairs. Use the dominant or median fragment size when a full distribution is unavailable.

Spectrophotometric purity ratio (A260/A280) of the amplified DNA measured after amplification and before sequencing preparation. Typical values near 1.8 indicate relatively pure DNA, though WGA products may vary.

Storage condition of the amplified DNA between completion of WGA and sequencing capture, such as frozen, refrigerated, or temporary ambient handling. This describes the material's post-process state, not the sequencing instrument configuration.

Whether the amplified DNA passed basic checks and was deemed ready for sequencing capture. Record this as a material-level readiness flag after amplification and prior to loading onto the sequencing platform.

ngs_capture.reasoning: For the ngs_capture Capture node, I included only measurement-session and instrument-configuration metadata for the sequencing run, plus hardware identification required for operation nodes. I excluded amplified DNA properties because those belong to the upstream entity, and I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the downstream sequencing_reads Signal node. The fields capture how the sequencing platform was configured and identified during acquisition so the raw reads can be traced to a specific instrument session.

md_schema.descr: Name of the sequencing platform used to measure the amplified DNA and generate raw reads, recorded for the capture session. Examples include Illumina MiSeq, Illumina NovaSeq, Ion Torrent, or Oxford Nanopore MinION.

Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for this capture session, recorded as the hardware vendor at run time. Examples include Illumina, Thermo Fisher Scientific, and Oxford Nanopore Technologies.
Model name or number of the sequencing instrument used for data acquisition, recorded during the capture session. Example formats include MiSeq, NovaSeq 6000, or MinION Mk1C.

Serial number of the sequencing instrument used for the capture session, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware instance. Use the exact manufacturer-assigned serial string, for example SN12345678.

Identifier for the specific sequencing run or capture session that produced the raw reads from this amplified DNA sample. Use the platform's native run identifier or an internal run label, for example RUN_2026_001.

Sequencing chemistry or reagent version used on the platform during this capture session, such as kit version or flow cell chemistry. Record the chemistry actually loaded for the run because it affects read quality and output characteristics.

Target read length in base pairs for this sequencing capture session, if the platform was configured with a specific read length. For short-read platforms this is often 50 to 300 bp; for long-read platforms it may be much larger. Record the configured target, not the final observed read length distribution.
Name or identifier of the operator who initiated or supervised the sequencing capture session. Record the responsible operator for traceability of the measurement session.

sequencing_reads.reasoning: For the sequencing_reads Signal node, I included only raw data artefact descriptors: file format, size, dimensions, storage location, and technical quality metrics that describe the read file itself. I excluded sequencing platform configuration and run-session details because those belong to the upstream ngs_capture node, and I excluded assembly or biological interpretation because those belong downstream to the assembled genome. The fields are limited to what a downstream user needs to locate, validate, and parse the raw reads.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw sequencing reads generated by the sequencing capture session. Common examples include FASTQ, BAM, or CRAM, depending on the platform and processing stage. This describes the artefact itself, not the sequencing instrument.
Size of the raw sequencing read file on disk in bytes, measured for the stored artefact. Typical values may range from megabytes to hundreds of gigabytes depending on sequencing depth and platform.

Total number of raw sequencing reads contained in the file, counted from the stored artefact after acquisition. Use the read count as represented in the raw data file, before assembly or substantial downstream filtering.
Total number of nucleotide bases represented across all raw reads in the file, measured in base pairs. This is a file-level content metric for the raw signal artefact, not a capture setting.

Average per-base quality score across the raw sequencing reads, computed as a technical quality metric for the stored file. Report the platform-standard quality score scale, typically Phred-like values.

Location or URI where the raw sequencing read file is stored, such as a local path, object storage URI, or repository accession. Example formats include file paths or accession strings used by the project.
Whether the raw sequencing reads are stored compressed or uncompressed as delivered in the dataset. This is a technical property of the file artefact rather than a biological or capture property.

assembly_process.reasoning: For the assembly_process Process node, I included only assembly-operation parameters, software identity, and immediate output-quality indicators for the genome reconstruction step. I excluded raw read file properties because those belong to sequencing_reads, and I excluded the assembled genome's size/completeness/contamination properties because those belong to the downstream assembled_genome Derivative node. Per the operation-node rule, I included the software agent details (name, version, repository) to support reproducibility. The fields focus on how the assembly was run and whether the assembly succeeded at a process level, not on the properties of the produced draft genome.

md_schema.descr: Name of the genome assembly software used to reconstruct the bacterial genome from sequencing reads. Record the exact tool name used in this process, for example SPAdes, MEGAHIT, or metaSPAdes.
Software version of the genome assembly tool used for this process. Record the release or build version exactly as executed, because assembly outcomes can vary across versions.

Repository, package source, or distribution channel for the assembly software used in this process. Examples include GitHub repository, Bioconda package, or vendor distribution. Record the source that identifies the exact implementation used.

Assembly algorithm or mode used by the software during genome reconstruction, recorded at the time of the process. Examples include de Bruijn graph, overlap-layout-consensus, single-cell mode, or metagenomic mode, depending on the tool.

k-mer size or set of k-mer sizes used during assembly, recorded as a process parameter. Typical values depend on read length and software, often spanning 15 to 141 for short-read assemblers. If multiple k values were used, report the primary or comma-separated set per project convention.

Minimum contig length threshold used during or after assembly, measured in base pairs. Typical values may range from 200 to 1000 bp depending on filtering policy. Record the threshold applied in this process step.

Immediate quality assessment of the assembly process outcome, such as successful, fragmented, low_coverage, or failed. Use this to capture the process-level result before the assembled genome derivative is characterized.

assembled_genome.reasoning: For the assembled_genome Derivative node, I included only computed-result metadata that characterizes the draft SAG produced by assembly: output dimensions, assembly quality indicators, and contig/scaffold statistics. I excluded assembly software and parameters because those belong to the upstream assembly_process node, and I excluded raw read file properties because those belong to sequencing_reads. The fields are intended to let a downstream user judge the completeness and usability of the reconstructed genome without duplicating process metadata.

md_schema.descr: Total assembled genome length in base pairs after genome reconstruction from sequencing reads. Typical SAG draft assemblies may range from hundreds of kilobases to several megabases. Record the final assembled span represented by the derivative.
Number of contigs in the assembled draft genome after assembly and any standard post-assembly filtering. This is a structural output metric for the derivative and indicates fragmentation level.

N50 contig length of the assembled genome in base pairs, computed from the final assembly. This is a standard output quality statistic for draft genome contiguity; higher values generally indicate more contiguous assemblies.

GC content of the assembled genome sequence, expressed as a percentage of total assembled bases. Typical bacterial genomes often fall within a broad range around 20 to 80 percent depending on taxonomy.

Estimated completeness of the assembled genome, reported as a percentage of expected single-copy marker content or equivalent genome completeness metric. This is a derivative-level quality indicator used to assess whether the SAG draft is sufficiently recovered.

Estimated contamination or redundancy level in the assembled genome, reported as a percentage. Use the project-standard contamination estimate derived after assembly to indicate mixed or duplicated genomic content in the draft SAG.

Overall quality class assigned to the assembled genome based on downstream assessment of completeness, contamination, and contiguity. Use the categorical label adopted by the project for draft SAG triage.
Location or URI where the assembled genome file is stored, such as a path to a FASTA file or repository accession. This identifies the derivative artefact itself and supports retrieval for reuse.
